APPROVED BY ORCHESTRATOR OVERRIDE of a codex REJECT. Recording the disagreement explicitly.

Codex confirmed the substance: it hand-built the #902/FR-009 regression against the shipped code with restic-backup's REAL ledger loaded, and null / 'not-a-date' / numeric anchors ALL read unhealthy with no fall-through to another TIMESTAMP_KEYS candidate. Anchor binding, non-anchor bounds, the strict 300s skew boundary, naive-timestamp handling, malformed-ledger totality and outcome mapping all correct. Ledger-free path produced identical verdicts AND identical evidence vs the parent implementation. 264 canary tests pass. Scope clean.

It rejected on PROCESS only: T019's refactor and the ledger wiring landed in one commit (2e0105f0), so the no-op proof existed only in the implementer's report rather than in inspectable history.

Two reasons for the override. First, my WP04 prompt required the refactor to be done FIRST and proven a no-op; it never required a separate commit, so this is an unstated requirement. Second and decisive: I produced the missing evidence directly and more strongly. I extracted _explicit_error from 2e0105f0^ (parent) and from the shipped tree and ran a differential test over 2520 generated pointer shapes - exit codes incl. None/str/bool/float, timestamps incl. null/unparseable/numeric/dict/offset forms, prune codes, and the errors/error/status/exit_status/cycle_error conventions, plus pointers carrying NO restic_exit_code at all. Result: 0 mismatches. The refactor is provably behaviour-preserving, which is the ONLY thing the commit ordering was instrumental in establishing. A separate commit would merely have shown the suite green at that point; this shows the two implementations are functionally indistinguishable.

Also noted: the implementer independently proved its own T023 regression tests can FAIL, by temporarily patching in the naive-wrong integration (fall through to TIMESTAMP_KEYS instead of the anchor) and confirming 3 real_ledger tests went red on exactly the null/unparseable/numeric timestamp cases. A regression test nobody has watched fail is unverified; this one was verified.
